title: Mercury retrograde, actually explained
caption: Mercury doesn't actually reverse. It's a passing-lane illusion, and astrology reads it as a pause, not a curse.

beats.head: Retrograde is an *optical illusion.*
beats.sub: From Earth, a planet seems to slide backward against the stars.

beats.head: Think of passing a car on the *freeway.*
beats.sub: For a moment, the slower car seems to roll backward.

beats.head: Here's Mars: Earth *overtakes* it on the inside lane.
beats.sub: And Mars traces a little loop in our sky.

beats.head: Mercury does it from the *inside* track.
beats.sub: It laps us, and the same illusion kicks in.

beats.head: It happens about *three* times a year.
beats.sub: Each one lasts roughly three weeks.

beats.head: In astrology, Mercury rules *messages.*
beats.sub: So retrograde reads as a time to slow down and double-check.

vis.name: Sam
msgs: wait, what did you mean by that

beats.head: It's not a *curse.* It's a pause.
beats.sub: Reread the text. Confirm the plan. Say what you meant.

beats.head: And no, it didn't make your ex *text.*
Send this to whoever blames *Mercury* for everything.
